clue.text: Rhino runs into deep

indicators.note: the runs are put into the word for deep, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deep voice is a bass
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros charges into deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' is old British slang for money, here meaning the slang word for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British slang words for money.

clue.text: Old money's governed contribution to winter sports

parts.note: bob was the slang for a shilling in old British money; plural bobs
to have governed is to have led

explanation.surface: Pre-decimal cash once governed what was given to winter sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobsleigh is a racing sled used in a Winter Olympic event.

clue.text: Warning: American service of poor quality after Republican's put in

indicators.note: the Republican is placed inside the other pieces, which is what put in signals

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A notice that a US tennis serve went wrong once a Republican was involved.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Spinner's first and best set of deliveries? It's not much of a break

definitions.text: It's not much of a break

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word for the spinner is taken

parts.note: the best is the top
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler's finest over, and the batting barely breaks free.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket setting makes 'break' look like a spinning ball's turn; it means a pause in a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a brief halt on a longer journey, so only a short break.

clue.text: Is engaged in air support, backing identification

indicators.note: going backwards, so the assembled pieces are read in the opposite direction
the word Is is held within the air, as if engaged in it

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
to support is to aid

explanation.surface: Something is busy in an air-support operation, helping to identify targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air support' reads as military aircraft, but 'air' is a tune and 'support' is help; 'backing' reverses everything once 'engaged in' has placed its piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the identification of an illness from its symptoms.

clue.text: Aspirations denied English: lots of whisky

indicators.note: the English letter is refused, so it is removed from the word for aspirations

parts.note: aspirations are hopes or dreams

explanation.surface: Hopes thwarted, an Englishman drowns his sorrows in a lot of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Drams are small measures of spirit, so several drams are lots of whisky.

clue.text: Condescension seen in poor-quality organ care

indicators.note: the words are badly treated, so their letters come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Snobbish disdain is shown in shoddy maintenance of a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is a haughty, superior manner, close in sense to condescension.

clue.text: Boy picked up methodology? That's not what appears

indicators.note: in a down entry, something picked up is lifted, so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a boy is a son
a methodology is how something is done

explanation.surface: A lad grabs a method; whatever it is, it is not what is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' works as an upward reading only because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is someone or something that fails to turn up as expected.

clue.text: Rebuilding of the pits? It's an arresting call

indicators.note: the words are reconstructed, so their letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Reconstruction of the coal mines makes a striking announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional cry to get a fleeing criminal arrested, so 'arresting' is a pun on catching.

clue.text: Very much left to express anger, having the wherewithal

parts.note: so means very much, as in so tired
to vent is to let out one's anger

explanation.surface: Someone very much inclined to rant now has the means to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvent means able to pay one's debts, having enough money.

clue.text: Senior abuse all over the place in capital

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Elder abuse is widespread in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Buenos Aires is the capital city of Argentina.

clue.text: Response to assault by left winger?

parts.note: ow is the cry someone gives when hit

explanation.surface: A footballer's reaction when a left-sided player fouls him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left winger' reads as a football or political position; 'winger' alone means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword shorthand: a winger is anything with wings, such as a bird.

clue.text: Some gambling facilities will accommodate motorcycle racing

indicators.note: the facilities will hold the racing inside them

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for a toilet, the loo in British slang
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Betting venues will host motorbike racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery game, one form of gambling.

clue.text: Acknowledge agreement on an intermittent basis?

definitions.meaning: formally commit to a contract by putting one's name to it
a broken line is intermittent, so writing on one is literally signing on an intermittent basis

explanation.surface: Assent is only given now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means formally agreeing by signing a contract where the space is marked.

clue.text: See 12
Cheers, securing a small religious building in Antipodean area

indicators.note: the word for cheers holds the other pieces safely within it

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a manse is a minister's house

explanation.surface: A toast while holding a little chapel somewhere in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea lies between Australia and New Zealand, the Antipodes.

clue.text: Representation of Mary, all round church, displaying tears

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the church abbreviation
a fresh rendering of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A statue of the Virgin Mary encircling a church weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representation of' rearranges MARY ALL into LARYMAL, which goes 'round' CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal means relating to weeping or tear glands.

clue.text: Weather that's damp, nothing less

indicators.note: means minus, so the nothing is taken away

parts.note: damp means moist
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Wet weather and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather that's damp' looks like the whole definition, but 'damp' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a weather condition of fine water droplets in the air.

clue.text: Stone handled by mason not initially under pressure

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

indicators.note: without its first letter, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a mason dresses stone, shaping it, so stone handled by one is dressed

explanation.surface: A stonemason works a block under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means strained or subjected to pressure.

clue.text: Member of privileged class is positive no longer

indicators.note: is no longer true means it was, so the present tense is replaced by the past

parts.note: is in the past tense becomes was

explanation.surface: Someone from the elite has stopped being optimistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Acronym for White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, the traditional American social elite.

clue.text: Let loose, stick around the marshes

definitions.note: plural in the clue, singular in the answer used as a mass noun for marshy land

indicators.note: the stick goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a wand is a thin stick

indicators.note: set free, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Release a rod to hang about the marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let loose' reads as one phrase, but 'loose' is the anagram signal on 'Let' and 'stick' then goes 'around' the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetland is marshy, waterlogged ground, the same as marshes.

clue.text: Series of clues provided about one in charge of laboratory work?

indicators.note: the trail goes around the one

parts.note: a scent is a trail of clues to follow
I is the Roman numeral one
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Clues are laid out around the lab head.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientific describes experimental work, the kind done in a lab.

clue.text: Some editor acknowledged heading up major arterial route

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters go upwards, read backwards
only part of the words is used, a hidden run of letters

explanation.surface: An editor admitted a major road was planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arterial route' sounds like a main road; it is the neck artery.
explanation.definitionFit: The carotid is the main artery in the neck supplying the head.

clue.text: Minister French are pushing higher, showing wit in Paris

indicators.note: in a down entry the pair moves up to the top

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
es is the French for are, as in tu es

explanation.surface: A clergyman's French counterparts climb up, showing Gallic humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is the French word for wit and liveliness of mind.

clue.text: Sobbing ahead of holiday for an opener

parts.note: sobbing involves tears
a holiday is a trip

explanation.surface: Crying before going on vacation as an opening move.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear strip is a band pulled to open a package.

clue.text: Reduced choice in containing a Nationalist agitation

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the other pieces inside
cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pick is a choice

explanation.surface: Limited options among a group of nationalists stir unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is a state of frantic alarm, a strong agitation.

clue.text: Composer lecturer included in retro fashion

indicators.note: the lecturer's letter is put inside
backward-looking, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rage is a fashion, all the rage

explanation.surface: A composer's teacher wears vintage clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Endless gluttony limiting black bird

indicators.note: the shortened word bounds the black letter, enclosing it
without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: gluttony is greed
B is the abbreviation for black in pencil grades

explanation.surface: Never-ending gluttony limits a dark bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving water bird.

clue.text: A singular and special fool

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: One remarkable idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a donkey means they are stupid, a synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Provoking memory regarding perfume sample?

parts.note: re means regarding or about
a sample of perfume is a miniature scent, a mini scent

explanation.surface: A perfume tester brings back old memories.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminiscent means suggestive of the past, calling things to mind.

clue.text: Solid Act I, lively, affecting the heartbeat

indicators.note: energetically moved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strong, energetic first act sets hearts racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastolic refers to the phase of a heartbeat when the heart refills.

clue.text: Be apprehensive about degree study

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Worrying about a course of study for one's degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread is to fear or anticipate with anxiety.
